experiences.name: Prague Castle Complex Tour
experiences.description: Explore the largest ancient castle complex in the world, including St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and Golden Lane. Walk through centuries of Bohemian history and enjoy panoramic views over Prague's red-roofed skyline.

experiences.name: Budapest Thermal Bath Experience at Széchenyi
experiences.description: Soak in one of Europe's largest and most iconic thermal bath complexes, built in 1913 in stunning Neo-Baroque style. Experience the Hungarian bathing culture that has been central to Budapest life for centuries, with multiple indoor and outdoor pools at varying temperatures.

experiences.name: Prague Old Town & Astronomical Clock Walking Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided walking tour through the medieval Old Town Square, witness the hourly show of the 600-year-old Astronomical Clock, explore the Jewish Quarter (Josefov), and discover Gothic churches and Baroque palaces that tell the story of Prague's layered past.

experiences.name: Budapest Danube River Night Cruise
experiences.description: Sail along the Danube River at night to witness the illuminated Hungarian Parliament Building, Buda Castle, and Chain Bridge in all their glory. This iconic cruise offers a breathtaking perspective on Budapest's UNESCO World Heritage riverside panorama.

experiences.name: Budapest Ruin Bar Crawl in the Jewish Quarter
experiences.description: Discover Budapest's unique ruin bar culture, born from abandoned pre-war buildings transformed into eclectic nightlife venues. Starting at the legendary Szimpla Kert, explore quirky interiors filled with vintage furniture, local art, and live music — a cultural phenomenon unique to Budapest.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Prague Václav Havel Airport at 22:30. Take the budget-friendly Airport Express bus (Line AE) to Náměstí Republiky for ~60 CZK (~$2.50 USD). Check into your accommodation, freshen up, and take a short night stroll around the Old Town Square if energy permits — it's beautifully lit at night.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a 24-hour convenience store or a kebab shop near the Old Town (~150 CZK / ~$6)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — only arrive and settle in. Prague's public transport is efficient and cheap. Validate your bus ticket to avoid fines. Exchange some currency at the airport kiosk or use a no-fee ATM for Czech Koruna (CZK).

day_by_day.morning: Start with a free self-guided walk through Prague's Old Town (Staré Město). Visit the iconic Astronomical Clock (Orloj) at the Old Town Hall — the hourly show is free. Wander through Týn Church courtyard and the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) exteriors for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Charles Bridge (free) and hike up to Prague Castle (Hradčany). Purchase the Circuit B ticket (~250 CZK / ~$11) which covers St. George's Basilica, Golden Lane, and the Daliborka Tower. Enjoy panoramic views over the red-roofed city.
day_by_day.evening: Descend into Malá Strana (Lesser Town) and explore the charming cobblestone streets. Visit Kampa Island along the Vltava River at sunset — completely free and scenic.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh pastry (trdelník or rohlik) from a local bakery near Old Town (~50 CZK / ~$2)
meals.lunch: Lokál restaurant chain — affordable Czech classics like svíčková (beef sirloin with cream sauce) for ~180 CZK (~$8)
meals.dinner: U Fleků brewery area or a local hospoda (pub) — try goulash with bread dumplings and a Czech beer for ~200 CZK (~$9)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Prague's cobblestones are uneven. The Castle district involves uphill walking. September weather in Prague is mild (15–20°C / 59–68°F), bring a light jacket for evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Vyšehrad Fortress (free entry to the grounds) — a lesser-visited but stunning hilltop fortress with a cemetery of famous Czechs, Romanesque rotunda, and sweeping views of the Vltava. Much less crowded than Prague Castle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Vinohrady and Žižkov neighborhoods — bohemian, local, and authentic. Visit the Žižkov Television Tower (~250 CZK / ~$11) for incredible city views and spot the famous crawling baby sculptures by David Černý.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center and visit the Wenceslas Square (Václavské náměstí) area — a historic boulevard where Czech history was made. Free to walk and explore.

meals.breakfast: Café Louvre-style budget alternative — try a local café near your hotel for coffee and toast (~80 CZK / ~$3.50)
meals.lunch: Manifesto Market (if open) or a food truck near Náměstí Míru — budget street food ~150 CZK (~$6.50)
meals.dinner: Restaurace Nota Bene or similar neighborhood restaurant in Vinohrady — hearty Czech meal for ~200–250 CZK (~$9–11)

day_by_day.notes: Vyšehrad is a hidden gem and far less touristy — highly recommended. The Žižkov TV Tower is one of Prague's quirkiest landmarks. Today's itinerary involves significant walking (10–12 km) — pace yourself.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning to revisit any Prague highlights or explore the Náplavka riverside farmers market (open Saturdays, but check for Friday events). Browse local stalls for fresh produce, artisan goods, and cheap street food.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the budget train or FlixBus from Prague to Budapest. The journey takes approximately 6–7 hours by train (RegioJet or Czech Railways + Hungarian Railways, ~$20–35 USD booked in advance) or 7 hours by FlixBus (~$15–25 USD). Enjoy the scenic Central European countryside.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Budapest (Keleti or Kelenföld railway station). Take the metro (Line M2 or M4, ~350 HUF / ~$1) to your accommodation area. Check in, freshen up, and take a short evening walk along the Danube riverbank — the Parliament building is illuminated at night and absolutely breathtaking.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Prague's main train station or a nearby bakery (~80 CZK / ~$3.50)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the train journey — buy supplies at a Tesco or Albert supermarket near the station (~100 CZK / ~$4.50)
meals.dinner: Upon arrival in Budapest, try a lángos (deep-fried dough with sour cream and cheese) from a street vendor near the station (~800 HUF / ~$2.20) — a classic Hungarian street food

day_by_day.notes: Book your Prague–Budapest transport in advance for the best budget prices. RegioJet offers affordable, comfortable trains with Wi-Fi. Validate your Budapest transit ticket immediately upon boarding. Hungary uses Hungarian Forint (HUF) — use a no-fee ATM or exchange at a bank.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a walk across the iconic Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) from Pest to Buda — free and spectacular. Hike up Castle Hill (Várhegy) to Buda Castle and the Royal Palace. Explore the castle grounds, Matthias Church, and the Fisherman's Bastion (exterior free, inner terrace ~1,000 HUF / ~$2.75).
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Pest and explore the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) — a stunning neo-Gothic iron market with fresh produce, Hungarian paprika, salami, and folk crafts on the upper floor. Budget-friendly and a cultural experience in itself.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) at sunset. Visit the haunting Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial (free) — a powerful WWII Holocaust memorial. Watch the Parliament building light up across the river.

meals.breakfast: Café near your Budapest accommodation — coffee and a kifli (Hungarian crescent roll) (~500 HUF / ~$1.40)
meals.lunch: Inside the Great Market Hall — try lángos or a warm goulash soup from a market stall (~1,500 HUF / ~$4.20)
meals.dinner: Karavan Street Food Court on Kazinczy Street (Ruin Bar district) — diverse affordable options from ~1,500–2,500 HUF (~$4.20–7)

day_by_day.notes: Castle Hill can be reached by foot, funicular (~1,200 HUF one way), or the free Castle Bus (Várbusz). September in Budapest is warm (18–23°C / 64–73°F) — perfect for walking. The Great Market Hall is closed Sundays, so this Saturday visit is perfectly timed.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building — one of the world's most beautiful parliament buildings. Book a guided tour in advance (~6,000 HUF / ~$16.50 for non-EU visitors) — absolutely worth the splurge. The interior is jaw-dropping.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Jewish Quarter (VII. District) — visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (Dohány utcai zsinagóga), the largest synagogue in Europe (~4,000 HUF / ~$11 with museum entry). Wander through the atmospheric ruin bars district (Romkocsmák) even during the day — Szimpla Kert opens for a Sunday farmers market.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Budapest's famous thermal bath culture at Széchenyi Baths — evening entry is often cheaper (~6,000–8,000 HUF / ~$16.50–22). Soak in the outdoor thermal pools under the stars — a quintessential Budapest experience.

meals.breakfast: Szimpla Kert Sunday farmers market (opens ~9am) — fresh local produce, homemade jams, and breakfast items (~1,000–1,500 HUF / ~$2.75–4.20)
meals.lunch: Hummus Bar chain — excellent value Middle Eastern food popular with locals (~1,800 HUF / ~$5)
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite before or after the thermal bath — try a nearby falafel wrap or pizza slice (~1,500 HUF / ~$4.20)

day_by_day.notes: Book Parliament tours online in advance — they sell out, especially on weekends. Bring a swimsuit and towel for Széchenyi Baths (or rent towels on-site for ~500 HUF extra). The ruin bars district is lively even on Sunday afternoons.

day_by_day.morning: Take Metro Line M1 (the oldest metro in continental Europe — a historic ride itself!) to Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) — free to visit. Explore Vajdahunyad Castle in City Park (Városliget) — free exterior, magical architecture combining Romanesque, Gothic, and Baroque styles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museum of Fine Arts (Szépművészeti Múzeum) adjacent to Heroes' Square — one of Central Europe's finest art collections (~3,200 HUF / ~$8.80). Alternatively, explore the House of Terror (Terror Háza) museum on Andrássy Avenue (~4,000 HUF / ~$11) — a sobering and essential museum about Hungary's 20th-century totalitarian regimes.
day_by_day.evening: Walk down the elegant Andrássy Avenue (a UNESCO World Heritage boulevard) toward the city center. Stop at the Hungarian State Opera House to admire the exterior (free) or check for affordable standing tickets for an evening performance (~1,000–3,000 HUF / ~$2.75–8.25 for standing room).

meals.breakfast: Local pékség (bakery) near your accommodation — fresh pogácsa (savory scone) and coffee (~600 HUF / ~$1.65)
meals.lunch: Ötkert or a nearby self-service étterem (canteen-style restaurant) — traditional Hungarian lunch menu (napi menü) with soup and main course (~2,000–2,500 HUF / ~$5.50–7)
meals.dinner: Belvárosi Lugas Étterem or similar traditional Hungarian restaurant — try chicken paprikash or stuffed peppers (~2,500–3,500 HUF / ~$7–9.70)

day_by_day.notes: The napi menü (daily lunch menu) at Hungarian restaurants is one of the best budget strategies — typically includes soup, main course, and sometimes a drink for a flat price. The House of Terror requires 1.5–2 hours minimum — emotionally intense but historically vital.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — revisit a favorite spot or explore Gellért Hill (Gellérthegy) for free. Hike up to the Citadella fortress and Liberty Statue for the best panoramic views of Budapest, the Danube, and both the Buda and Pest sides. Completely free and stunning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at the Great Market Hall area or along Váci Street (tourist street — compare prices). Pick up Hungarian paprika, Tokaji wine, or Unicum liqueur as affordable gifts. Do a final café stop in a classic Budapest coffeehouse (kávéház) — try the New York Café exterior or a budget alternative like Centrál Kávéház.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport (Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport) via the 100E airport bus (~900 HUF / ~$2.50 from Deák Ferenc tér) or by taxi (~7,000–9,000 HUF / ~$19–25). Allow 2–2.5 hours before departure for check-in and security.

meals.breakfast: Final Hungarian breakfast — try rántotta (scrambled eggs) with fresh bread at a local café (~1,200 HUF / ~$3.30)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the city center before heading to the airport — sandwich or salad from a local deli (~1,500 HUF / ~$4.20)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or pack snacks — airport food is pricier, so grab supplies from a convenience store before departing (~2,000 HUF / ~$5.50)

day_by_day.notes: Keep your transit card loaded for the airport bus. Allow extra time on the last day for any delayed transport. Total estimated budget for the full 8-day trip (excluding flights and accommodation): approximately $250–350 USD per person, covering transport between cities, entry fees, meals, and local transit. Prague is cheaper than Budapest overall — plan heavier spending in Prague for cultural sites.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Václav Havel Airport Prague at 22:30. Take the Airport Express bus or a pre-booked taxi to your accommodation. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest to prepare for the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night bite near the hotel – look for a 24-hour convenience store or a nearby kebab/pizza spot for something light before bed

day_by_day.notes: Flight UA arrives at 22:30. Do not schedule any sightseeing tonight. Pre-arrange airport transfer in advance to avoid stress upon late arrival. Exchange some currency or withdraw Czech Koruna (CZK) from an ATM at the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a leisurely breakfast, then head to Prague Old Town (Staré Město). Explore the iconic Old Town Square, admire the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) and watch the hourly chime show. Wander through the medieval lanes and visit the Church of Our Lady before Týn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the legendary Charles Bridge, taking in the Baroque statues and panoramic views of the Vltava River. Climb up to Prague Castle (Pražský hrad) – explore St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and Golden Lane. Enjoy sweeping views over the city's red rooftops.
day_by_day.evening: Descend into the Malá Strana (Lesser Town) neighborhood for dinner. After dinner, take a romantic evening stroll along the illuminated Charles Bridge and riverside promenade.

meals.breakfast: Café Savoy or a local bakery near the hotel – try a traditional Czech pastry (koláč) with coffee
meals.lunch: Lokál Dlouhááá – a beloved mid-range Czech pub serving authentic svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) and fresh Pilsner Urquell on tap
meals.dinner: Café de Paris in Malá Strana – known for its signature butter herb sauce schnitzel; mid-range and very satisfying

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – Prague Castle hill involves a significant uphill walk. Purchase a Prague Castle ticket online in advance to skip queues. The Astronomical Clock show runs every hour on the hour.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Josefov, Prague's historic Jewish Quarter. Explore the Jewish Museum complex, which includes six synagogues (Pinkas, Maisel, Spanish, Old-New Synagogue) and the hauntingly beautiful Old Jewish Cemetery – one of the oldest in Europe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Vinohrady or Žižkov neighborhood for a more local Prague experience. Visit the striking Žižkov Television Tower (with crawling baby sculptures by David Černý) for panoramic city views. Explore the quirky street art and bohemian cafés of this up-and-coming district.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert – Prague is famous for its evening Mozart and Dvořák performances held in historic venues like the Municipal House (Obecní dům) or Rudolfinum. Book tickets in advance.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café – try chlebíčky (open-faced sandwiches), a classic Czech morning staple
meals.lunch: Eska – a celebrated mid-range restaurant in Žižkov/Karlín offering modern Czech cuisine with seasonal ingredients and excellent sourdough bread
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Café Imperial – a stunning Art Nouveau dining room serving traditional Czech and Central European dishes at mid-range prices

day_by_day.notes: Jewish Museum tickets should be booked online – they sell out quickly in September. The Television Tower observation deck has a small café inside. Evening concerts typically start at 19:00 or 20:00 – check schedules at praguetickets.com.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning day trip to Kutná Hora (about 1 hour from Prague by train). Visit the extraordinary Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church) – a small chapel decorated with the bones of approximately 40,000 people, a truly unique and sobering historical site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the rest of Kutná Hora's UNESCO-listed historic center. Visit the magnificent St. Barbara's Cathedral, a Gothic masterpiece rivaling Prague's St. Vitus. Stroll through the charming medieval town center and the Italian Court (Vlašský dvůr), the former royal mint.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Prague by train in the late afternoon. Spend the evening exploring the Nusle or Vinohrady neighborhoods, known for their Art Nouveau architecture and vibrant local bar scene. Pack your bags tonight for the Budapest journey tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Prague's Hlavní nádraží (main train station) before departure – grab a coffee and pastry to go
meals.lunch: Lunch in Kutná Hora at Pivnice Dačický – a charming local pub in a historic building serving hearty Czech meals (goulash, roast pork) at very reasonable prices
meals.dinner: Back in Prague – try Restaurace U Fleků, a historic brewery and restaurant dating to 1499, serving dark lager brewed on-site and traditional Czech dishes

day_by_day.notes: Trains from Prague Hlavní nádraží to Kutná Hora run regularly; journey is about 55–65 minutes. Buy round-trip tickets in advance via Czech Railways (cd.cz). The Ossuary is a short walk or taxi from Kutná Hora train station. Begin packing for Budapest departure tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of your Prague accommodation. Take the morning train or bus from Prague to Budapest (approximately 7–8 hours by RegioJet or FlixBus, or ~6.5 hours by train via Brno). Enjoy the scenic Central European countryside along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest in the late afternoon. Check into your accommodation and freshen up. Take a gentle orientation walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) on the Pest side to get your bearings and enjoy the first views of Buda Castle across the river.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant ruin bar scene in the Jewish Quarter (VII District). Visit Szimpla Kert – Budapest's most famous ruin bar – for a drink and to soak in the eclectic, artistic atmosphere. Wander Kazinczy Street for more options.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast near your Prague hotel or at the train/bus station before departure
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and sandwiches for the journey, or purchase food on board the RegioJet train (they have a bistro car)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Budapest's Jewish Quarter – try Mazel Tov, a stylish mid-range restaurant in a stunning open-air ruin setting, serving Israeli-Mediterranean fusion with Hungarian touches

day_by_day.notes: Book Prague–Budapest transport well in advance – RegioJet trains offer comfortable seats with entertainment and food service. Arrive Budapest Keleti or Kelenföld station depending on route. Get Hungarian Forints (HUF) from an ATM upon arrival. Budapest's VII District is very walkable.

day_by_day.morning: Begin with Buda Castle Hill. Take the historic Funicular (Budavári Sikló) up from Clark Ádám Square. Explore the Royal Palace (Hungarian National Gallery), Matthias Church with its stunning Zsolnay tile roof, and the Fisherman's Bastion for breathtaking panoramic views over the Danube and Pest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the iconic Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) on foot back to Pest. Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building – book a guided interior tour in advance to see the Holy Crown of Hungary and the stunning Neo-Gothic interior. Stroll along the UNESCO-listed Danube Promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a traditional Hungarian thermal bath evening. Head to Széchenyi Thermal Bath in City Park – open until 22:00, it's magical in the evening with lit pools and a relaxed atmosphere. A quintessential Budapest experience.

meals.breakfast: New York Café or a nearby bakery – try lángos (deep-fried flatbread with sour cream and cheese) from a street vendor near the Castle District
meals.lunch: Halászbástya Restaurant near Fisherman's Bastion – mid-range with stunning views; try Hungarian fish soup (halászlé) or grilled pike-perch
meals.dinner: Borkonyha Winekitchen – a Michelin-recommended mid-range restaurant near the Parliament serving modern Hungarian cuisine paired with excellent local wines

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours must be booked online at jegymester.hu well in advance – Sunday slots fill up fast. Bring a swimsuit, towel, and flip-flops for Széchenyi Baths, or rent them on-site. The Funicular is a fun but short ride – buy tickets at the bottom station.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (Dohány utcai zsinagóga) – the largest synagogue in Europe and a deeply moving historical and cultural landmark. Explore the adjacent Hungarian Jewish Museum and the Memorial Garden with its weeping willow Holocaust memorial.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore City Park (Városliget) and Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) – an impressive Millennium Monument showcasing Hungarian history. Visit the Museum of Fine Arts or the newly renovated Ethnography Museum. Rent a rowboat on the City Park lake or simply relax in this beautiful green space.
day_by_day.evening: Take a Danube River cruise at sunset – a wonderful way to see Budapest's illuminated bridges and skyline from the water. Several operators offer 1–2 hour evening cruises departing from Vigadó Square. After the cruise, explore the lively Gozsdu Udvar courtyard for nightcaps.

meals.breakfast: Café Gerbeaud on Vörösmarty Square – a legendary Budapest coffeehouse; try their Dobos torte (layered chocolate-caramel cake) with a cappuccino
meals.lunch: Karavan Street Food Court on Kazinczy Street – an outdoor collection of food trucks offering Hungarian and international street food at budget-friendly prices; try chimney cake (kürtőskalács)
meals.dinner: Onyx Restaurant (set menu option) or Mák Bistro – upscale-leaning but accessible mid-range modern Hungarian cuisine; alternatively, Kiosk Budapest for river-view dining at reasonable prices

day_by_day.notes: The Great Synagogue is closed on Saturdays; Monday is a great day to visit. Book the Danube cruise in advance through Legenda or Silverline Cruises – sunset cruises (around 19:00–20:00 in September) are especially beautiful. Gozsdu Udvar is a covered passage filled with bars and restaurants.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest – visit the Central Market Hall (Nagy Vásárcsarnok), a stunning 19th-century iron-and-tile market hall. Browse stalls selling paprika, Tokaji wine, salami, embroidered textiles, and folk crafts. Pick up last-minute souvenirs and local food gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through the upscale Andrássy Avenue – Budapest's answer to the Champs-Élysées – toward the Opera House. If time allows, take a quick tour of the Hungarian State Opera House (one of Europe's most beautiful). Visit the House of Terror Museum on Andrássy Ave for a sobering but essential look at Hungary's 20th-century history under both Nazi and Soviet regimes.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Budapest. Head to the airport or train station for onward travel. Reflect on an incredible 8-day journey through two of Central Europe's most magnificent cities.

meals.breakfast: Final Hungarian breakfast at Molnár's Kürtőskalács or a local pékség (bakery) – grab fresh pastries and coffee for the road
meals.lunch: Upper floor of the Central Market Hall – try lángos or a hearty Hungarian stew at one of the market's casual eateries with great atmosphere
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Spíler Budapest in Gozsdu Udvar – a lively, stylish mid-range bistro with a broad menu of Hungarian and European dishes; great for a celebratory final meal

day_by_day.notes: The Central Market Hall closes around 15:00–17:00 on weekdays – go in the morning. The House of Terror is emotionally intense but historically invaluable – allow 1.5–2 hours. Budapest Liszt Ferenc Airport is about 30–40 minutes from the city center by taxi or 100E bus. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in and security.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives late evening
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Václav Havel Airport Prague at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to your hotel in the heart of Prague. Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome nightcap at the hotel bar. Light late-night room service to settle in comfortably.

meals.breakfast: On board or at airport
meals.lunch: On board or at airport
meals.dinner: Late-night premium room service at hotel — charcuterie board, fine Czech cheese selection, and a glass of Moravian wine

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Request early check-in amenities such as chilled champagne and turndown service. Keep Day 1 light — rest is essential for the days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start with a gourmet breakfast at the hotel. At 10:00, embark on a private guided walking tour of Prague's Old Town (Staré Město) — explore the iconic Astronomical Clock (Orloj) on the hour, stroll through Old Town Square, and admire the Gothic Týn Church. Your expert guide provides rich historical context on Bohemian history and medieval Prague.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the legendary Charles Bridge on foot, pausing to admire the 30 Baroque statues and sweeping Vltava River views. Ascend to Prague Castle (Pražský hrad) — the largest ancient castle complex in the world. Private guided tour of St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and the Golden Lane. Enjoy panoramic views over the red-roofed city.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to refresh. Dinner reservation at a Michelin-recommended Prague restaurant such as Field or La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise — indulge in modern Czech tasting menus paired with premium wine. After dinner, take a romantic evening stroll across Charles Bridge illuminated by lantern light.

meals.breakfast: Elaborate hotel breakfast buffet with made-to-order eggs, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at Café Savoy in Malá Strana — Art Nouveau interiors, Czech classics like svíčková and duck confit
meals.dinner: Tasting menu at La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise — 7-course modern Bohemian cuisine with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book Prague Castle private tour in advance to skip public queues. Best photos on Charles Bridge are taken in the early morning or evening light. Comfortable walking shoes strongly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Private morning tour of the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) — one of the best-preserved Jewish historical districts in Europe. Visit the Old Jewish Cemetery, the Spanish Synagogue, and the Pinkas Synagogue with its haunting Holocaust memorial. A deeply moving and culturally significant experience with a specialist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the vibrant Vinohrady and Žižkov neighborhoods — discover Art Nouveau architecture, boutique galleries, and local artisan shops. Visit the National Museum (Národní muzeum) on Wenceslas Square, recently restored to its full Neo-Renaissance grandeur, for an immersive journey through Czech natural and cultural history.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a world-class classical music or opera performance at the Prague State Opera (Státní opera) or the Estates Theatre — one of Europe's most beautiful opera houses where Mozart himself conducted. Pre-performance champagne reception in the grand foyer. Post-show, unwind with a nightcap at a sophisticated Prague cocktail bar such as Black Angel's Bar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast with fresh fruit, yogurt, artisan breads, and specialty Czech honey
meals.lunch: Lunch at Lokál Dlouhááá — acclaimed Czech gastropub with unpasteurized Pilsner Urquell on tap and elevated traditional dishes
meals.dinner: Pre-opera dinner at Kampa Park — riverside fine dining with European cuisine and exceptional wine cellar overlooking the Vltava

day_by_day.notes: Book opera or concert tickets well in advance — September is peak cultural season in Prague. Smart evening attire recommended for the opera. Jewish Quarter tours are emotionally impactful — allow time for reflection.

day_by_day.morning: Optional: Sunrise hot air balloon flight over the Bohemian countryside outside Prague for a breathtaking aerial perspective (seasonal availability). Alternatively, a private morning visit to the Lobkowicz Palace inside Prague Castle — home to one of the finest private art collections in Europe including original Beethoven and Mozart manuscripts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day excursion to Kutná Hora (1 hour from Prague by private car) — a UNESCO World Heritage town. Visit the extraordinary Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church), decorated with the bones of approximately 40,000 people, and the magnificent Gothic Cathedral of Saint Barbara. Return to Prague by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Prague at Alcron Restaurant (Radisson Blu Alcron Hotel) — legendary Art Deco fine dining institution. Enjoy the chef's signature seafood tasting menu. After dinner, a private sunset cruise on the Vltava River with champagne and canapés as a perfect send-off from Prague.

meals.breakfast: Light hotel breakfast before morning excursion — fresh juices, pastries, and espresso
meals.lunch: Lunch in Kutná Hora at Piazza Navona — charming Italian-Czech fusion restaurant near the cathedral
meals.dinner: Tasting menu at Alcron Restaurant with sommelier-selected wine pairing — Prague's most celebrated fine dining experience

day_by_day.notes: Private car hire for Kutná Hora is strongly recommended over public transport for comfort and flexibility. The Bone Church is unlike anything else in Europe — prepare for a surreal experience. Pack bags tonight for early departure to Budapest tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Prague hotel after a leisurely breakfast. Private luxury transfer to Praha hlavní nádraží (Prague Main Station) for the premium Railjet or EuroCity train to Budapest Keleti — approximately 6.5 to 7 hours, with scenic Central European countryside views. Alternatively, a private charter flight (~1 hour) can be arranged for ultimate luxury.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest in the early-to-mid afternoon. Private transfer to your luxury hotel in Budapest. Check in and freshen up. Begin gentle exploration of the immediate Pest riverbank — stroll along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) and admire the iconic Parliament Building across the water. Stop for coffee and cakes at the legendary Gerbeaud Café on Vörösmarty Square.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner reservation at Costes Downtown or Onyx Restaurant — Budapest's Michelin-starred fine dining flagships. Experience contemporary Hungarian haute cuisine in elegant surroundings. After dinner, take a short walk to see the Chain Bridge (Széchenyi lánchíd) and Buda Castle dramatically illuminated at night.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet hotel breakfast in Prague before checkout
meals.lunch: Premium dining car on the train — or packed luxury picnic hamper arranged by the hotel with Hungarian salami, artisan cheeses, and local wines
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred dinner at Onyx Restaurant — modern Hungarian tasting menu with exceptional Hungarian wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: First-class train tickets should be booked well in advance. The train journey itself is scenic and relaxing — a premium experience in its own right. Budapest hotel concierge should be briefed on dietary preferences prior to arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Royal Palace and Buda Castle District — explore the medieval cobblestone streets, Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom) with its stunning Zsolnay tile roof, and the Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) for the most spectacular panoramic views of the Danube, Pest, and the Parliament Building. One of Europe's finest urban panoramas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Danube to Pest via private car. Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) — one of the world's most beautiful legislative buildings — on an exclusive private tour including access to the Hungarian Crown Jewels. Afterward, explore the Great Market Hall (Nagy Vásárcsarnok) for premium Hungarian products: Tokaj wine, paprika, foie gras, and handcrafted souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Budapest's famous thermal spa culture: private evening session at the opulent Széchenyi or Gellért Thermal Baths — grand Neo-Baroque pools fed by natural geothermal springs. Afterward, dinner at Babel Budapest — a celebrated contemporary restaurant showcasing seasonal Hungarian ingredients with artistic presentation.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Hungarian specialties including lángos, fresh pastries, cold cuts, and Tokaj wine-infused preserves
meals.lunch: Lunch at Rivalda Café & Restaurant inside the Buda Castle District — elegant setting with Hungarian and international cuisine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Babel Budapest — innovative modern Hungarian cuisine with natural wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours require advance booking and may have security protocols — arrange through hotel concierge. Bring swimwear for the thermal baths. The evening spa experience is quintessentially Budapest and not to be missed.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (Dohány utcai zsinagóga) — the largest synagogue in Europe and second largest in the world. Explore the adjacent Hungarian Jewish Museum and the haunting Memorial Garden. Continue to the Hungarian State Opera House (Magyar Állami Operaház) for an exclusive backstage tour of this Neo-Renaissance architectural masterpiece.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Budapest's vibrant ruin bar culture and the trendy 7th District (Jewish Quarter) with its eclectic street art, design shops, and galleries. Visit the House of Terror (Terror Háza) — a powerful and sobering museum documenting Hungary's 20th-century totalitarian regimes under both Nazi and Soviet rule. A deeply important historical experience.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset dinner cruise on the Danube aboard a luxury riverboat — sail past the illuminated Parliament, Chain Bridge, Buda Castle, and Matthias Church with a private chef, champagne, and Hungarian folk music. The most spectacular way to experience Budapest's legendary nighttime skyline — a UNESCO World Heritage panorama.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast with made-to-order omelets, Hungarian salami, fresh fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Kiosk Budapest — stylish bistro near the Elizabeth Bridge with seasonal European cuisine and Danube views
meals.dinner: Private luxury Danube dinner cruise — 4-course Hungarian-inspired menu with Tokaj wine and champagne

day_by_day.notes: Book the private dinner cruise well in advance — this is one of Budapest's most sought-after premium experiences. The House of Terror is emotionally intense — allow adequate time and mental space. Opera House tour should be booked through concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Last-minute stroll through the elegant Andrássy Avenue — Budapest's grand Champs-Élysées-style boulevard lined with Neo-Renaissance mansions, luxury boutiques, and embassies. Stop at the iconic Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) and the adjacent City Park (Városliget) for a peaceful final morning in the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to hotel for checkout and luggage collection. Depending on departure time: optional visit to the Museum of Fine Arts (Szépművészeti Múzeum) near Heroes' Square — housing one of Central Europe's finest collections of Old Masters. Private luxury transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Budapest — carry the memories of two extraordinary Central European capitals, rich in history, culture, and imperial grandeur.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell hotel breakfast — full Hungarian spread with champagne toast to celebrate the journey
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Gerloczy Café in the heart of Pest — Viennese-style café with Hungarian classics in a beautiful historic setting
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or on-board — hotel can arrange a premium farewell gift hamper with Hungarian wines and delicacies

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for airport transfer and check-in. Ask hotel concierge to arrange a premium farewell hamper with Tokaj wine, Hungarian salami, and local chocolates as a beautiful trip memento. Confirm all transfers 24 hours in advance.
